name: Raymond T. White
current_role: Co-founder & Managing Director, Legion Partners Asset Management; director of NN Inc., Clear Channel Outdoor and Lifecore Biomedical
profile: Raymond T. 'Ted' White co-founded Legion Partners (2012), a Los Angeles long-only activist fund focused on North American small caps. Earlier he was Director of Corporate Governance at CalPERS and COO of European activist Knight Vinke. He joined Clear Channel Outdoor's board in Jan 2024 and NN Inc.'s in Jan 2026 via a Legion cooperation agreement.
interesting_fact: At CalPERS he ran the entire corporate-governance program, including $3 billion in active management, proxy voting and focused engagement, before switching sides to become an activist investor.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as an Investment Officer / Deputy State Treasurer in the California State Treasurer's Office doing fixed-income trading, and later co-chaired the ICGN Executive Remuneration Committee (to Dec 2014) and sat on the PCAOB Standing Advisory Group.
notes: Goes by 'Ted White'. Board seats come via Legion Partners activism; firm's general email is the published route. NN appointment: https://www.nninc.com/?p=4834

name: Bernard Shek
current_role: Chief Legal Officer and Secretary, Sandisk Corporation
profile: Bernard Shek is Sandisk's Chief Legal Officer and Secretary (since the Feb 2025 spin-off from Western Digital), overseeing global legal, compliance, IP and government affairs. A litigator with ~30 years advising semiconductor and tech companies, he joined Sandisk in 2011 as a litigation leader and later served as a deputy general counsel at Western Digital after it acquired Sandisk.
interesting_fact: He has effectively come full circle: joined SanDisk in 2011 in litigation (Senior Director, then VP of Litigation), stayed through Western Digital's 2016 acquisition, and now runs legal for the re-spun-off, independently listed Sandisk.
deep_cut_fact: A Bay Area local product: BA from UC Berkeley (1994) and law degree from UC Hastings (now UC College of the Law, San Francisco, 1997).
notes: Low public profile in-house lawyer; no personal social presence found. Education/dates from aggregator + Justia lawyer directory, so treat deep-cut as moderately sourced. Best route is Sandisk media relations.

name: Jason VanWees
current_role: Vice Chairman, Teledyne Technologies (retiring effective Feb 1, 2027)
profile: Jason VanWees joined Teledyne in 1999 after investment banking at Goldman Sachs and Salomon Brothers, and became Vice Chairman in Oct 2021, overseeing strategy, acquisitions and investor relations. Teledyne announced in Sept 2026 that he will retire effective Feb 1, 2027, with Mary Grace DeForest taking over IR and M&A.
interesting_fact: He led Teledyne's acquisition of 75 complementary businesses for cumulative consideration of about $12.8 billion, as sales grew from roughly $750 million to $6.5 billion during his tenure.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for an M&A dealmaker, he trained as a scientist: his Stanford B.S. is in Chemical Engineering and Biological Sciences.
notes: Retiring Feb 2027, which may make him more available for a podcast. Contact via Teledyne investor relations (see Teledyne press releases).

name: Pedro Arnt
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, dLocal (NASDAQ: DLO); board member, Allegro.eu
profile: Pedro (Dornelles) Arnt spent 24 years at MercadoLibre, serving as CFO for over a decade (c.2011-2023) as it became Latin America's largest e-commerce and fintech company. He joined Uruguay-founded emerging-markets payments firm dLocal as co-CEO in Aug 2023 and later became sole CEO; he also sits on Allegro.eu's board.
interesting_fact: He joined MercadoLibre in November 1999, just three months after it was founded, when it had roughly 20 employees, and stayed through its growth into one of Latin America's most valuable companies.
deep_cut_fact: Before MercadoLibre he worked at Boston Consulting Group; he holds a magna cum laude bachelor's from Haverford College and a master's from the University of Oxford.
notes: Frequent podcast guest (Fintech Leaders, Stratechery, Baillie Gifford 'Invest in Progress', Founder's Mentality) - receptive to long-form interviews on emerging-markets payments.

name: Kyle G Hranicky
current_role: Senior Executive Vice President and CEO of Commercial Banking, Wells Fargo & Company; member of the Operating Committee
profile: Kyle Hranicky has spent his whole banking career at Wells Fargo, joining in 1995 as a commercial banking analyst and rising through loan syndications, the Energy Group, Corporate Banking and Middle Market Banking. Since Sept 2021 he has run Commercial Banking, serving companies with $25M-$2B in sales and a loan book of more than $350B. Houston-based; joined the ABA board in Oct 2025.
interesting_fact: Earlier in his Wells Fargo career he headed the bank's Energy Group, a direct link to the podcast's energy theme, and he remains based in Houston.
deep_cut_fact: Before banking he worked for the Southland Corporation (the then-parent of 7-Eleven); he holds a UT Austin BBA and an honors MBA from Thunderbird, and is in the McCombs School of Business hall of fame.
notes: Corporate executive; outreach best via Wells Fargo corporate communications/newsroom (newsroom.wf.com). Energy-group background makes him a natural fit for energy-finance topics.

name: Ashish Arora
current_role: President and Chief Executive Officer, Cricut, Inc. (director since March 2021)
profile: Ashish Arora has led Utah-based Cricut, maker of smart cutting machines and design software for DIY crafters, since February 2012, taking it public on Nasdaq in 2021 and building a subscription base of roughly 3 million paid subscribers. He previously was a general manager at Logitech (digital home software and products) and spent eight years at financial software/analytics firms.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Cricut shifted from a craft-tool maker to a connected-platform business, with millions of paying subscribers to its Design Space software and AI design features layered on its machines.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011, while at Logitech and a year before joining Cricut, Digital Media Wire named him one of its '25 Executives to Watch in Digital Entertainment'. He trained as an engineer at Thapar Institute before a University of Kansas MBA.
notes: Input lists name reversed as 'Arora Ashish'. Contacts per Cricut 2026 press releases (media: Avani Patel).

name: Robert C Abernethy
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Peoples Bancorp of North Carolina and Peoples Bank; President, Secretary & Treasurer, Carolina Glove Company (Newton, NC) [assuming Robert C. Abernethy Sr.]
profile: Robert C. Abernethy Sr. (74 in 2025) has been a director of Newton, NC-based Peoples Bancorp since 1976 and chairman since 1991, and is its largest individual holder (~6.6%). He runs family business Carolina Glove Company, a glove manufacturer, and is an officer of paving firm Midstate Contractors.
interesting_fact: He has chaired the community bank for more than three decades (since 1991) after joining its board in 1976, giving him nearly 50 years of banking experience alongside running a glove manufacturer.
deep_cut_fact: He is a graduate of the N.C. Bank Directors' College and attended its very first Advanced Directors' Training session, run with NC State's College of Management.
notes: AMBIGUOUS: two directors share the name - Robert C. Abernethy Sr. (chairman since 1991) and Robert C. Abernethy Jr. (43, EVP of Carolina Glove, Catawba County commissioner, director since Dec 2024). SEC insider name lacks suffix; profile assumes Sr. (the larger holder). Very private, local-business profile; route via the bank's corporate secretary.

name: James G Hinkle
current_role: Director, Home BancShares, Inc. (Centennial Bank), Conway, Arkansas; member, Arkansas State Police Commission
profile: James G. Hinkle (77) is a veteran Arkansas community banker: president of the Bank of Mountain View from 1981 to 2005 and of Mountain View BancShares from 1995 until it merged into Home BancShares in 2005, when he joined Home BancShares' board. He chaired Bank of Mountain View until its 2009 merger into Centennial Bank and now sits on the audit/risk and nominating committees.
interesting_fact: His wealth stems from selling his Ozarks hometown bank holding company into Home BancShares, which has since grown into one of the South's larger regional banks (Centennial Bank).
deep_cut_fact: A committed conservationist: he served on the Arkansas Game and Fish Commission (1996-2003) and was a director of the National Wild Turkey Federation from 2003 to 2018.
notes: Low-profile rural Arkansas banker; no personal online presence found. Outreach via Home BancShares investor relations/corporate secretary.
